name: Carmo Church
short: A Baroque-Rococo church of 1756–1768 with a huge side panel of azulejos laid in 1912.
long: The Church of the Venerable Third Order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel was built in 1756–1768 to a design by José Figueiredo Seixas for the Carmelite Third Order. It is famous for its side façade, covered entirely in azulejos of 1912 showing scenes from the founding of the Carmelite Order. Next to it stands the Igreja dos Carmelitas, and between the two is wedged the “Casa Escondida”, a hidden house barely a metre and a half wide.
history:
The Carmelite Third Order received a plot west of the Igreja dos Carmelitas in 1752. Because two churches could not then be built right next to each other, a narrow “Casa Escondida” (Hidden House), a little over a metre and a half wide, was built between them — still counted among Porto’s narrowest buildings. The church itself was built in 1756–1768 to a design by the architect José Figueiredo Seixas; the order’s hospital was finished later, in 1801.

The façade is crowned by a relief of Saint Anne, patron of the order, who according to the chronicles appeared to a group of early Carmelites; she is also the church’s patron. In the niches flanking the entrance are the prophets Elijah and Elisha, two central figures of the Carmelite tradition. The upper tier is decorated with pinnacles and statues of the four Evangelists, betraying the influence of the “Italian Baroque” of Nicolau Nasoni.

The church’s chief glory is its side façade, clothed entirely in azulejos. The composition was designed in 1912 by Silvestre Silvestri, painted by Carlos Branco and executed in the “Senhor do Além” and “Torrinha” factories in Vila Nova de Gaia. The panel depicts scenes linked to the founding of the Carmelite Order and to Mount Carmel.

Inside are rich gilded carving in the side chapels and the high altar, statues and oil paintings. The iconographic programme centres on the Passion of Christ: the Agony in the Garden, the Arrest, the Flagellation, the Lord in the Crown of Thorns, Ecce Homo and the Way of the Cross, ending with the Crucifixion on the high altar and the Resurrection on the ceiling.

On 3 May 2013 the Carmo church was declared a national monument together with the neighbouring Igreja dos Carmelitas. In recent years the order has opened its heritage to visitors: a tourist circuit runs through the Casa Escondida, the church, the small catacombs, the noble hall, the sacristy and the vestments room, with part of the ticket price funding restoration.
facts: Built in 1756–1768 to a design by the architect José Figueiredo Seixas.
The side façade is covered in azulejos of 1912: designed by Silvestre Silvestri, painted by Carlos Branco, made in the “Senhor do Além” and “Torrinha” factories in Vila Nova de Gaia.
The church’s patron is Saint Anne; the prophets Elijah and Elisha stand in the niches of the façade.
Between Carmo and Carmelitas is wedged the “Casa Escondida”, about 1.5 metres wide.
The order’s hospital was completed in 1801.
Declared a national monument on 3 May 2013 together with the Igreja dos Carmelitas.
tip: The azulejo side façade faces Rua do Carmo — don’t miss it; many visitors only see the main portal. The order’s tourist circuit costs €3.50 and the Casa Escondida €2. Bear in mind the services (daily at 9:30 and 15:00) and the rosary at 14:30, when the full circuit closes.
